ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The lotus feet of the Divine function as the absolute foundation and shelter for devoted seekers, replacing worldly reliance with complete surrender to grace. Simran (loving remembrance) finds its only stable ground in this sacred presence, which sustains and anchors the soul. This teaching instructs the mind to abandon false supports and rest exclusively in divine refuge.

Themes: divine refuge, lotus feet, total surrender, spiritual foundation, steadfast reliance, soul’s anchor, grace as sustenance
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
The prayer anchors loving remembrance (simran) upon the lotus feet (divine presence and refuge) within the heart, seeking shelter in the perfect Guru. This inward fixation pleads for grace while actively dissolving worldly attachment (maya), replacing distraction with sustained communion. The practice trains the mind to dwell in sacred proximity, converting internal awareness into a steady sanctuary of devotion.
Themes: inner devotion, divine refuge, guru guidance, heart-centered meditation, spiritual surrender, grace, steadfast focus, sacred presence
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
Declares that anchoring the mind on the lotus feet of the Divine cultivates a lasting practice of loving remembrance (simran) and surrender. This stance instructs the seeker to replace maya with devoted attention, transforming consciousness until it mirrors the saints’ unwavering focus on the Creator. It describes the resulting peace of a heart permanently fixed on divine presence.

Themes: divine love, loving remembrance, saintly consciousness, mental discipline, surrender, spiritual habit, transcending worldly distraction
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
Instructs the mind to board the vessel of the Lord’s Lotus Feet, using that sacred refuge to cross the turbulent ocean of maya (worldly attachment) and attain liberation. This image frames complete surrender to the divine presence as the only reliable passage beyond earthly suffering. Anchoring awareness in the Guru’s guidance, the seeker escapes rebirth and reaches enduring spiritual freedom.

Themes: divine refuge, spiritual crossing, surrender to the Guru, liberation from samsara, overcoming maya, inner transformation, eternal peace
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
Anchoring the mind in the lotus feet (divine presence and total refuge) dissolves maya (worldly attachment), making only the Lord’s sovereignty truly sweet. This statement declares a transformed consciousness, instructing the heart to sustain simran (loving remembrance of the divine Name), while rejecting every other craving. True fulfillment arrives when surrender replaces distraction, and the soul finds satisfaction solely in God’s grace.
Themes: divine refuge, mind anchoring, maya rejection, simran, exclusive devotion, spiritual satiety, sovereign grace
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
Drinking the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name) via simran (loving remembrance) brings total inner contentment and confers immortality past bodily decay. The Guru delivers this spiritual sustenance, elevating mortal life into an ageless, deathless state immune to grief. The teaching praises grace as the exclusive path to enduring peace, directing devotees to abandon earthly cravings for constant devotion, thus guaranteeing final liberation from pain.
Themes: spiritual nourishment, divine grace, eternal life, freedom from suffering, loving remembrance
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥: Ingesting the nectar of naam (the divine Name) produces spiritual intoxication that shatters the snares of maya (worldly attachment). This practice of simran (loving remembrance) breaks karmic chains, dissolves ego, and grants permanent liberation from cyclic suffering. Internalizing sacred sound achieves this absolute freedom. Themes: naam, simran, maya, liberation, intoxication, bondage, ego
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
The mind is urged to drink the Ambrosial Nectar, a concrete image for naam (the divine Name). This simran (loving remembrance) quenches spiritual thirst, grants eternal vitality, and dissolves maya (worldly attachment). Partaking in this sacred sustenance transforms mortal consciousness into abiding refuge, aligning human purpose with divine communion.
Themes: naam, simran, ambrosial nectar, spiritual sustenance, inner transformation, liberation from maya, divine presence, mindful surrender
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
An imperative instruction to internalize divine presence by drinking the nectar of the Lord’s essence, treating loving remembrance (simran) as essential spiritual nourishment. Seeking refuge in the Perfect Guru activates continuous chanting of the divine Name (naam), converting passive faith into active sustenance. This directive frames mortal life as a deliberate intake of grace, where repeated simran quenches earthly longing with perpetual communion.

Themes: divine nourishment, guru refuge, naam simran, sacred nectar, inner transformation, devoted remembrance, soul’s sustenance
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
The Guru pours the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name) into the seeker’s mouth, transforming spiritual death into awakened life. This declaration addresses the inner self, testifying how simran (loving remembrance) resurrects the dormant soul from worldly attachment. Internalizing the sacred word reverses existential decay and restores true consciousness.
Themes: spiritual resurrection, guru’s grace, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), inner awakening, liberation from spiritual death, transformative devotion
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The divine Name (naam) acts as an immortalizing nectar and boundless treasury, delivering spiritual sustenance that erases mortality. This passage commands assembling in the company of the devout (sangat) to absorb this essence through loving remembrance (simran). Pursuing this inner wealth communally anchors the soul in timeless grace, displacing fleeting worldly attachment (maya) with permanent liberation.
Themes: naam, simran, sangat, immortality, spiritual nourishment, communal devotion, liberation from mortality, transcendence of maya
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
Divine grace breaks the wheel of cyclic existence, pairing the concrete image of a shattered cycle with permanent liberation that erases the terror of mortality. This declaration praises the soul’s final release from samsara (the cycle of birth and death), affirming that true refuge ends all karmic return. Surrender yields enduring peace beyond worldly attachment.

Themes: liberation from samsara, divine mercy, freedom from rebirth, eternal peace, breaking the cycle of mortality, spiritual refuge, transcending worldly attachment
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Unshakable equanimity through simran (loving remembrance) secures direct communion with the Divine, functioning as refuge and liberation. This steady awareness dissolves terror of mortality, shields the soul from spiritual decay, ensuring eternal safety. Jam (the angel of death) embodies both physical end and egoic stagnation, yet this dread vanishes when surrender to the naam (the divine Name) ensures lasting peace.
Themes: equanimity, divine union, fearlessness, spiritual immortality, loving remembrance, surrender, liberation
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
Meditating on the servant’s sacred hymn within sangat (the company of the devout) severs the lifelong dread of rebirth and dissolution, anchoring the soul in eternal refuge. Loving simran (loving remembrance) of the divine Word dissolves the cycle of suffering, replacing mortal anxiety with unshakable peace. This devotion breaks the chain of cyclic existence, granting liberation through steadfast alignment with the Guru’s teaching.
Themes: liberation from birth and death, loving remembrance, company of the devout, severing worldly fear, divine refuge, cyclical suffering, steadfast devotion
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Constant simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine throughout waking hours dismantles the concrete cycle of birth, aging, and death, embodying existential dread. This practice anchors consciousness in eternal presence, dissolving mortal terror and freeing awareness from cyclical suffering. Steady devotion neutralizes mortality’s grip, transforming temporal anxiety into unshakable peace. The teaching instructs seekers to fix attention on naam (the divine Name), declaring that continuous remembrance eradicates the fear of dying and rebirth.
Themes: simran, mortality, existential fear, liberation, divine remembrance, cyclical existence, mental peace, spiritual instruction
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
This declaration proclaims liberation from the cycle of rebirth, severing the suffering of birth and death while dissolving the terror of the Messenger of Death. The messenger embodies existential dread and karmic entrapment, which vanish through the company of the devout (sangat) and loving remembrance (simran). It functions as a promise of salvation and an instruction to abandon cyclical suffering for permanent spiritual freedom.
Themes: liberation from samsara, freedom from death anxiety, divine refuge, sangat, simran, cessation of suffering, spiritual surrender, breaking karmic cycles
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
This declaration describes a state of fearlessness achieved through surrender, using the image of fears washing away to signal complete refuge in the Divine. It proclaims the end of existential dread, replacing terror of cyclic existence with unshaken calm. Through simran (loving remembrance), the mind releases anxiety over mortality and rests in permanent liberation from rebirth.
Themes: fearlessness, liberation from rebirth, surrender, dissolution of dread, eternal peace, transcendence of mortality, devoted trust.
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Instructing seekers on the path to devotion, taking shelter in the saadh sangat (the company of the devout) provides refuge and spiritual guidance, actively cultivating divine love and surrender to the Creator. Holy fellowship catalyzes spiritual awakening, drawing the soul toward God through shared devotion. Righteous companionship transforms isolation into sacred attachment, ensuring loving remembrance flourishes among the spiritually aligned.

Themes: spiritual companionship, divine love, refuge, devotion, soul alignment, sacred attachment, loving remembrance
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Seeking refuge in the saadh sangat (the company of the devout) turns holy association into a crossing vessel for the world-ocean of cyclical suffering. This fellowship severs the noose of death, dismantling karmic bonds that enforce mortality. Through shared devotion, worldly attachment dissolves, liberation becomes certain, and the soul escapes rebirth. The text instructs seekers to treat saintly communion as the direct mechanism for breaking bondage and securing permanent release.
Themes: saadh sangat, world-ocean, noose of death, karmic bondage, liberation, holy fellowship, escape from rebirth, spiritual refuge
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Human purpose lies in holy fellowship; this teaching instructs seekers to embrace the saadh sangat (the company of the devout) as the direct path to divine union. The gathering of devotees becomes a conduit for grace, dissolving ego, anchoring the heart in the naam (the divine Name), and securing eternal refuge. Sacred community transforms isolation into communion.

Themes: saadh sangat, divine union, spiritual fellowship, ego dissolution, naam remembrance, eternal refuge, human purpose
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
Demonstrates how permanent attachment to sat sangat (the company of the devout) paints the spirit in radiant divine love and triggers ceaseless praise. Remaining in holy fellowship sustains loving remembrance, converts solitary seeking into shared devotion, and proves that communal worship actively manufactures unwavering connection to the Divine.
Themes: sat sangat, communal devotion, divine love, loving remembrance, spiritual transformation, ceaseless praise, holy fellowship
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
A supplication asks the Divine to draw the mind from vice and plant it in the sangat (company of the devout). The imagery of extraction and planting signifies spiritual rescue and refuge. Grace repeatedly pulls consciousness from maya (worldly attachment) and anchors it in sacred fellowship, redirecting attention from fleeting desires to enduring devotion, establishing simran (loving remembrance) as the only stable ground.
Themes: divine grace, spiritual extraction, mind fixation, sangat, maya, simran
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
The command to listen intently frames the sangat (the company of the devout) as a shared space and living refuge where collective remembrance dissolves ego and aligns the mind with divine truth. Acting as direct instruction, it urges communal devotion over isolation. By equating sacred fellowship with liberation, it positions attentive participation in the holy congregation as the sole pathway to grace.

Themes: sangat (the company of the devout), collective remembrance, ego dissolution, divine truth, sacred fellowship, spiritual liberation
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
Positions the Guru, the spiritual guide and divine manifestation, as the tangible refuge of Parameshwar, the Supreme Lord who actively dispels suffering and bestows lasting tranquility. This affirmation operates as recognition and surrender, positioning the mentor as the direct source of divine comfort and liberation from worldly anguish. Equating the human teacher with transcendent reality anchors devotion in absolute trust, ensuring that alignment with this sacred presence yields enduring peace and freedom from distress.

Themes: divine embodiment, spiritual refuge, inner tranquility, guru devotion, liberation from suffering, transcendent reality, surrender
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
Declares the Divine as the sole architect of existence and fountainhead of grace, affirming that every creature’s origin, sustenance, and fortune flow from one pervasive presence. This proclamation functions as devotional anchoring, redirecting trust from ego toward the benevolent designer who breathes life into all forms and dispenses mercy without bias. Recognizing this sovereign provision cultivates humility and steady reliance on the unseen hand that shapes fate.

Themes: divine providence, creative sovereignty, omnipresence, grace and mercy, devotional surrender, fate and destiny, humble reliance, benevolent design
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
Pleading for darshan (the direct vision and presence of God) from the boundless wellspring of mercy, the text supplicates for spiritual liberation through surrendered devotion. That sacred gaze trades worldly bondage for eternal freedom, exchanging mortal limitation for immortal grace. Only by resting in the Divine presence does the seeker achieve true redemption.
Themes: divine compassion, darshan, spiritual liberation, devotional surrender, grace, eternal freedom, refuge
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
Direct praise declares the Divine as the sovereign Master who overflows with every virtue and harbors a deep, compassionate heart. Such affirmation grounds the seeker in total surrender by establishing absolute divine completeness. The treasure of excellence signifies infinite moral perfection, while profound empathy guarantees unending mercy and spiritual abundance.

Themes: divine sovereignty, infinite virtues, profound compassion, devotional praise, spiritual abundance, absolute completeness, inner depth, masterful grace
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
Identifies the Divine as the sustainer of all life, deploying the mortal mouth to demonstrate that human speech cannot encompass infinite grace. This rhetorical question functions as an admonition to drop performative praise and embrace silent awe, since no tongue can quantify the Creator’s boundless giving. Genuine devotion accepts that mortal vocabulary consistently falls short of describing limitless mercy.
Themes: divine sustenance, inadequacy of human praise, silent reverence, surrender through humility, boundless generosity, devotional awe
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
The seeker stands overwhelmed by the boundless divine virtues, asking how any finite tongue can enumerate them, while affirming the Creator as the sovereign Master and living treasury of virtue, where the chest imagery signals divine abundance and complete refuge. This questioning functions as a devotional discipline, redirecting the mind toward humble simran (loving remembrance). Recognizing the divine as the inexhaustible chest of grace transforms enumeration into surrender, making every utterance an act of sanctuary within infinite excellence.

Themes: divine virtues, infinite praise, humble surrender, sacred remembrance, devotional awe, sovereign grace, transformative wonder
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
Warns the deluded seeker that the household offers no enduring refuge, declaring that no relative will shelter you even momentarily at death’s threshold. This admonition dismantles reliance on maya (worldly attachment) and kinship networks, reiterating that temporal protection evaporates completely. It asserts that mortal homes cannot anchor the spirit, redirecting attention to simran (loving remembrance) as the permanent sanctuary.
Themes: impermanence of worldly relationships, mortality and death, rejection of material shelter, spiritual independence, transience of human bonds, divine refuge
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
Admonishes the wavering mind to cease hesitation, pairing the concrete image of mental instability with the reality of divine provision. This instruction replaces worldly anxiety with unwavering trust, teaching that lasting peace emerges only when maya (worldly attachment) surrenders to the Creator’s promise. Anchoring awareness in naam (the divine Name) dissolves doubt, ensuring that steadfast devotion guarantees complete fulfillment.
Themes: steadfast trust, divine fulfillment, mind discipline, surrender, detachment from illusion, inner certainty, loving remembrance
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
Commands the restless mind to turn inward and practice simran (loving remembrance) of the Creator. Urges attention to rest in the shelter of the Divine, claiming divine refuge rather than chasing worldly distraction. Calls the intellect to chant the naam (the divine Name) and vibrate upon the sovereign Lord, establishing that peace arrives only when awareness fixes on the eternal source. Declares devoted meditation as the essential purpose of human existence.
Themes: simran, naam, inner focus, divine refuge, spiritual discipline, human purpose, mind training, devotion
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
Directing the mind, this passage halts futile wandering in forests or worldly realms, declaring the divine treasure resides within. It commands abandoning external quests for peace to recognize the indwelling presence of God as the source of bliss. Attention must turn inward, affirming that simran (loving remembrance) and true refuge emerge only when desire stops projecting outward and rests where the naam (divine Name) dwells.
Themes: internal divinity, cessation of external seeking, indwelling presence, inner refuge, redirection of attention
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
The figure of a staring madman embodies the mind’s captivity when it fixates on maya (worldly attachment) instead of seeking refuge in naam (the divine Name). It admonishes the restless intellect for mistaking transient spectacle for substance, warning that such fixation guarantees spiritual disorientation and wastes human potential. Urgent instruction demands immediate wakefulness, urging a pivot to simran (loving remembrance) so perception may clear and life may serve its true design.
Themes: spiritual delusion, maya, naam, simran, admonition, awakening, human purpose
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
Admonishes the listener to abandon pride and embrace radical humility. Become the dust beneath the lotus feet of devotees practicing simran (loving remembrance), for surrendered service alone unlocks divine union. This stance demands total self-abnegation, placing the seeker as the lowest attendant among the spiritually awakened. Liberation follows when personal ego dissolves into alignment with the naam (divine Name) upheld by the sangat (company of the devout).
Themes: humility, ego dissolution, simran, sangat, divine union, self-abnegation, spiritual surrender
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
The satguru (True Guru) nadar (divine glance of grace) operates as both a visual metaphor for divine attention and a vow of surrender, declaring that supreme contentment arises exclusively from merciful sight rather than material pursuit. This statement admonishes worldly craving, affirms that lasting peace flows solely through benevolent favor, and restates that complete fulfillment depends entirely on compassionate regard.
Themes: divine grace, guru devotion, inner fulfillment, spiritual surrender, transcendent joy, merciful attention
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
The True Guru (the embodied presence of divine grace) serves as a perceptual sieve that filters out suffering, ensuring that worldly trials never register as agony. This instruction admonishes the anxious mind to abandon its habit of magnifying hardship, declaring that divine mercy neutralizes anguish and restores unshakable equanimity. When compassionate awareness dominates, pain dissolves and the soul rests in permanent relief.

Themes: divine grace, transformation of suffering, spiritual perception, inner equanimity, guru’s mercy, dissolution of anguish
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
The fourth circle of the sacred marriage vow signifies total surrender, where divine grace dissolves mental agitation and produces sahaj (spiritual equilibrium). This statement declares that merging with the Beloved Lord steadies the soul, transforms frantic longing into quiet presence, and actualizes the goal of eternal communion.
Themes: divine union, surrendered devotion, inner stillness, grace-bestowed peace, soul’s steadiness, marital covenant, transcendent belonging
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
Welcoming the satguru (the True Guru) into the heart’s inner chamber establishes a sanctuary of refuge where simran (loving remembrance) replaces worldly striving. This declaration affirms that heart-centered surrender guarantees lasting tranquility, fulfills every sacred aspiration, and anchors the seeker in unshakable stillness. Devoted alignment with the guiding presence dissolves all lack and secures permanent contentment.
Themes: inner peace, guru devotion, spiritual fulfillment, heart-centered remembrance, divine grace, liberation from want, steadfast contentment
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
Declares the True Guru as an eternal refuge who actively severs the root of sorrow. This stance of surrender relies on divine grace, where loving remembrance (simran) dissolves maya (worldly attachment) and grants lasting peace. Cutting down suffering’s banner signifies permanent liberation from grief, establishing the Guru as a constant helper who uproots pain and sustains the devotee.
Themes: divine refuge, uprooting sorrow, eternal support, surrender, liberation, grace, steadfastness
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
The teaching commands seizing the present instant as the exclusive gateway to divine communion. It frames mortal life as a narrow threshold where maya (worldly attachment) yields to naam (the divine Name), converting ordinary awareness into darshan (sacred audience) and simran (loving remembrance). It warns against delay, treating each breath as a portable altar for cosmic reunion and surrender. It treats this fleeting chance as permanent alignment, urging immediate devotion.
Themes: divine union, present-moment urgency, spiritual opportunity, surrender, naam simran, transcendence of maya, sacred presence, immediate devotion
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
Earthly life operates as a marketplace where the mortal trades temporal moments for the profit of naam (the divine Name), coupling the commercial image with the underlying concept of spiritual acquisition. This instruction directs the human mind toward its sole objective: cultivating simran (loving remembrance) as the only viable return on existence. Every breath converts worldly passage into spiritual yield, because prosperity remains rooted in communion with the Creator.
Themes: human purpose, spiritual harvest, naam, simran, earthly existence, divine communion, mortal duty, eternal wealth
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
Instructs the seeker to join the sangat (company of the devout) and anchor simran (loving remembrance) in the heart, merging the image of rooted cultivation with the spiritual act of internalizing devotion. Declares that steadfast bhakti (devotional worship) alone secures divine grace, guarantees liberation, and functions as the only reliable refuge, because unwavering love for the Divine presence remains the sole path to salvation.
Themes: spiritual refuge, inner transformation, devotional practice, divine grace, liberation, sacred fellowship, steadfast remembrance
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
Declares that mortal existence finds lasting purpose only through simran (loving remembrance) of the divine Name. Clutching naam (the divine Name) like a lifeline grounds transient breath in eternal presence. This steady devotion replaces worldly striving with lasting peace, showing success comes when the mind rests perpetually on the Creator.
Themes: simran, naam, eternal life, successful living, divine remembrance, spiritual anchoring, transcendence of maya
